- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) mid-horizon, model frequently underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period volatility — add 1–2% upward adjustment for days 25–30 if sentiment is volatile or positive.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–4% downward buffer in early forecast days (1–5) to account for risk aversion.
